keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row for 1945-1947 and its Republic of Korea shape starts 1948). The page's area and population are blank; Cliopatria's Republic of Korea shape of 1948 is the nearest outline, so no area comparison could be made.

ledger.note: September 1945: the US Army takes over the south. 'from 9 September 1945 to 15 August 1948'; US troops stationed 8 September 1945; the 38th parallel was chosen on 11 August 1945 by two US Army planning officers 'for dividing the former Japanese colony into Soviet and American' zones; Japan surrendered 15 August 1945. The page calls the zone 'the southern half'.

region.text: the southern half of Korea below the 38th parallel: 'the official ruling body of the southern half of the' peninsula; Cliopatria's Republic of Korea outline of 1948 is the best match

ledger.note: 15 August 1948: the Republic of Korea is proclaimed in the south. The page does not describe a formal transfer of authority.

certainty.note: The 38th parallel was a surveyed line chosen on 11 August 1945 (page); the Ongjin and Kaesong exceptions of 1948 are not on the page.

sources.title: United States Army Military Government in Korea
sources.note: 9 September 1945-15 August 1948; Hodge; 38th parallel on 11 August 1945; Moscow conference December 1945; elections 10 May 1948; Republic 15 August 1948.

notes: Colony (occupation zone) filling the 1945-48 gap: Cliopatria has no Korea between the Empire of Japan's row and the 1948 republics. The ROK dossier (jk-02-d) starts at 1948-08 with the United States as predecessor and does not mention this authority; the US dossier (am-07) should carry the occupation_start (counterpart empire-of-japan) at 1945-09. The page is silent on the area, population and the Japanese forces' surrender dates beyond 15 August and 9 September 1945. The Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea and the People's Republic of Korea are listed as predecessors in the infobox; no page opened gives them territory, so they are not dossiers.
